I am 52 years old, farming 12 mu in Liudazhai village, Nanliyue township, Quzhou County. I finished middle school and have been managing this land for 5 years. My husband and children work off-farm in Handan, so I make the farm decisions myself. I hire a machine for rotary tillage before wheat sowing and for harvest, but I handle the irrigation and spraying.

Last year my wheat gave me 1,150 jin per mu and my maize gave 1,232 jin per mu. This year I will do almost the same thing, because changing what works is risky.

For wheat, I will rotary till the soil and sow 30 jin of improved Luyuan 502 seed per mu around September 15th. Before sowing, I will spread 100 jin of special compound fertilizer — the 18-22-5 kind — as basal. That is 50 kilograms per mu. In March, when the wheat turns green, I will broadcast another 40 jin of urea per mu as topdressing. Counting it all, that is about 18.2 kilograms of pure nitrogen, 11 kilograms of phosphorus, and 2.5 kilograms of potassium per mu. I know that is a bit more than what some people say, but my neighbor cut back last year and her wheat was shorter than mine. I will irrigate four times using my well: once in winter and three times in spring. I will spray insecticide three times, herbicide once, and fungicide twice. I expect about 575 kilograms per mu.

For maize, right after wheat harvest in early June, I will plant Denghai 605 hybrid seed using no-tillage direct seeding, 1.3 packages per mu. I will put down 100 jin of special compound fertilizer, the 27-6-7 type, as basal. That gives about 13.5 kilograms of nitrogen, 3 kilograms of phosphorus, and 3.5 kilograms of potassium per mu. I will not add urea topdress for maize — the compound costs 130 yuan per bag already, and last year the yield was good without it. I will irrigate twice in summer, spray insecticide three times, herbicide twice, fungicide three times, and plant regulator once to keep the stalks from falling over. I expect about 616 kilograms per mu.

I watch my costs carefully. The seed dealer wanted me to buy a more expensive maize variety, but I told him my maize did fine last year. I also thought about buying a new sprayer, but the old one still works. If I spend too much on fertilizer, I have less for pesticide and hired labor, so I keep the balance. But I will not cut fertilizer to save money — a bad harvest is a disaster I cannot afford.
